stem: In the context of Infantile Spasms, when is Vigabatrin considered the first-line treatment of choice?

options.text: When the spasms are classified as idiopathic or cryptogenic
When the patient is older than 12 months at onset
When there is a diagnosis of Tuberous Sclerosis
When the EEG shows focal centrotemporal spikes

explanation: Vigabatrin is specifically indicated as the primary treatment for infantile spasms when they occur in children with Tuberous Sclerosis.
rationale: Identify the neurocutaneous disorder that changes the standard treatment protocol for spasms.

optionExplanations.A: In idiopathic cases with no known cause, high-dose prednisolone is typically the preferred initial therapy.
optionExplanations.B: Vigabatrin's status as a first-line agent is tied to a specific underlying etiology rather than the age of the patient.
optionExplanations.C: Vigabatrin is specifically indicated as the primary treatment for infantile spasms when they occur in children with Tuberous Sclerosis.
optionExplanations.D: Centrotemporal spikes are characteristic of SeLECTS, where anti-seizure medication is often not required at all.
